findings.issue: Five turns spent locating Gracile's handler-context type definition, searching three wrong package paths before reaching @gracile/server/dist/route.d.ts
findings.suggestion: When verifying a package's API, go directly to the package's own dist/*.d.ts or its exports map rather than rg-ing across the workspace

findings.issue: First draft referenced an undefined constant and the wrong variable; rewritten immediately after self-review
findings.suggestion: Re-read the draft once before writing the file rather than right after; the error was caught 30 seconds later either way

findings.issue: Route file was first written with an incomplete duplicate-handler placeholder and fully rewritten in the next turn
findings.suggestion: Compose the complete file before invoking write; partial-file writes that are immediately replaced are pure waste

findings.issue: Test run prefixed with a meaningless `cd /home/ubuntu; cd /Users; cd /workspace` chain (guessing at paths that don't exist)
findings.suggestion: Just run `cd /home/agent/work && npm test`; the cwd was known from turn 1's pwd output

findings.issue: The agent itself identified that a localStorage team with no cookie would render the wrong toggle label server-side until client sync, but neither verified nor handled it
findings.suggestion: Cheap mitigation: set the cookie on document.client entry if the store is non-empty, or accept the gap explicitly; either way a one-line change or a quick browser probe would have closed it

summary: A tight, linear 26-turn session: requirements and architecture (cookie-mirrored team state for flash-free SSR) were settled before any code, the framework API was verified against the installed package's types, and the single test failure was root-caused and fixed in one cycle with the full suite re-run to green afterwards. The only waste was careless first drafts of two files and a scattered hunt for a type definition — roughly four turns of slack in an otherwise exemplary run.
